where: Section 2, rows rule and fill rule
problem: The row count is written as "2n rows" and "all 2n assignments". Read literally this means 2 times n, which is wrong: a formula with n variables has 2ⁿ rows (worked example 1 itself writes 2² = 4). A student copying "2n" will lose marks.
fix: With n variables there are 2ⁿ rows. Two variables use 4 rows; three variables use 8 rows. ... Fill the variable columns with all 2ⁿ assignments.
